Recommendation Blocks

I built the company's product recommendation feature from zero. A three-tier trust ladder let merchants start with high certainty and graduate as confidence grew; 80%+ of merchants who trialled Smart tier adopted it.

80%+ adoption, Smart tier5 regions · 200ms p99built on the platform ↑

Node.js · Redis · MongoDB Atlas (multi-region) · ClickHouse · Google Pub/Sub

My Role

What I personally owned

Product architecture — designed three-tier trust model (Manual/Automated/Smart) to reduce merchant risk and enable gradual adoption
System design — architected multi-region serving, latency SLAs, and real-time ranking engine
Core implementation — architected and directed the Redis-backed live tier, MongoDB serving layer, and ranking algorithm; team built and scaled
Adoption strategy — worked with sales/success to position tiers, built tier progression measurement and ROI tracking

What the product achieved

80%+ Smart-tier adoption — among merchants who trialled the tier
Multi-region latency — 200ms p99 across five regions with real-time ranking
Merchant trust — low-friction trust ladder moved from "risky feature" to default-on

Context

ConvertCart's merchants are SMBs running e-commerce stores. They need product recommendations but are risk-averse: wrong recommendations hurt conversion, cost credibility. If a feature feels unreliable or slow, they turn it off and never come back. Building merchant trust is the core product challenge.

Problem

ConvertCart doesn't have recommendations. Competitors do. Our merchants need this feature, but want low risk. How do you get a merchant to enable a feature that could hurt their business if it fails? How do you measure success without visibility into merchant behavior? How do you serve real-time ranking across five regions under 200ms?

BEFORE
  • No recommendations
  • Merchant anxiety about feature risk
  • No multi-region serving
WHY IT MATTERED
  • Merchants want to increase AOV
  • Market expects recommendations
  • Feature adoption = retention signal

Architecture

Three-tier ladder: Manual (CSM hand-picks products for each store), Automated (rules-based: "people who bought X also bought Y"), Smart (live behavioral ranking). Each tier uses different computation: Manual is static, Automated is batch-refreshed, Smart is real-time Redis-backed. Merchants graduate as trust builds. Multi-region MongoDB for serving, ClickHouse for analytics.

Key Decisions

  1. Three-tier trust model, not one
    Merchants graduate in order, not all-or-nothing. Manual tier proves value, Automated tier proves reliability, Smart tier proves sophistication.
  2. Computation matched to tier, not uniform
    Manual is static, Automated is batch, Smart is live. Allows gradual adoption without building all three systems at once.
  3. Redis-first for latency, durability trade-off
    In-flight sessions lost on Redis failure is acceptable for recommendations; would not accept this for orders.
  4. Read replicas trade freshness for speed
    Few seconds of lag serving non-US shoppers beats permanently slow blocks. Asymmetric failure modes.

Execution

Adoption Measurement

Built tier progression tracking to measure which merchants enabled each tier and how adoption changed over time. The available result: 80%+ of merchants who trialled Smart tier adopted it; timeframe and trial count are not published here.

Conversion Attribution

Built linkage from orders to specific recommendation blocks. This is what let merchants see ROI. Became the core proof point in sales conversations.

Multi-Region Challenge

The serving target was 200ms p99 across five regions: US, EU, APAC, India, and Brazil. Redis replication lag could produce stale rankings, so I used eventual consistency with cached-result fallback when replicas lagged. The page stayed responsive at the cost of slightly older data.

Impact

80%+ ADOPTION
Of merchants who trialled, 80%+ graduated to Smart tier

Why It Mattered

  • Recommendations became first-party product, not third-party tool.
  • Conversion attribution proved ROI to merchants.
  • Feature expanded into multi-channel personalisation.
  • Recommendation attribution gave Sales and Customer Success a concrete ROI story for merchant conversations.

Scale

80%+ Smart-tier adoption among trial merchants · five regions · 200ms p99 serving target · attribution used in merchant ROI conversations

What I'd Change Today

What I'd Preserve

The three-tier model was right. Trust-based adoption beats feature-push adoption.

What I'd Change

Would invest more in A/B testing infrastructure early (Smart tier had minor bugs that could have been caught faster). Also would have built more merchant-facing dashboards to show performance data in product, not just to sales/success.
